To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the synthesis and secretion of RBP by primary cultures of hepatocyte cells are maintained by supplementing the culture media with amino acids and by adding dexamethasones, but are not affected by addition of retinol.
primary cultures of hepatocyte cells from normal rats secrete RBP at a relatively high rate for the first 24 hr of culture, and then secrete at a low rate.
the synthesis and secretion of RBP by hepatocytes are regulated by the hormones dexamethasome, glucagon, and retinol.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and secretion of retinol binding protein (RBP), an essential transport protein for retinol, in primary cultures of rat liver cells.
the effects of various nutritional and hormonal factors upon the metabolism of retinoic acid (RA) by primary cultures of hepatocyte cells.
the metabolism and transport of retinol in the body.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dexamethasome and retinol, acting together or independently, regulate the synthesis and secretion of RBP by the liver.
the liver synthesizes RBP in response to the needs of the body, and that the synthesis is regulated by the nutritional state of the animal and by glucocorticoid hormones.
dexamethasome, in combination with a complete amino acid mixture, maintains the synthesis and secretion of RBP by normal hepatocytes in primary culture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dexamethasome, but not glucagon or retinol, can maintain RBP production and RBP secretion by cultured rat hepatocytes.

the liver is a major site for the synthesis and secretion of RBP and that the rate of RBP production is influenced by nutritional and hormonal factors, but the liver does not regulate RBP production by a retinol‐dependent mechanism.
the rate of RBP production and its secretion are controlled by a number of factors, including amino acids, hormones, and the availability of retinol.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the hepatocytes are capable of producing and secreting RBP, transtyretin, and other proteins at physiological rates in culture, and that the addition of amino acids and glucocorticoids to the culture medium maintains the cells in a healthy, active metabolic state.
RBP production and/or secretion can be maintained in primary cultures of hepatocyte for several days.
hepatocytes in culture can maintain RBP production and RBP secretion for several days if the culture medium is supplemented with both amino acids and dextramethasone.
